 Chery Omoda 5 recalled after broken rear axle incidents
 Following the publication of images of the Chery Omoda 5’s rear axle falling out, the SUV has been recalled in Australia due to potentially “insufficient welds”.
 by 
 Jordan Mulach 
 Published 
 November 16, 2026
 Link copied! 
 Copy failed! 
 Chery Omoda 5 with its rear axle torn out. Image credit: BitAuto 
 Chery Australia has recalled 7285 examples of the Omoda 5 SUV, following concerns the SUV’s rear axle could become disconnected from the car.
 As first published by BitAuto last month, an Omoda 5 owner in Malaysia was driving their car when the rear axle completely detached from the SUV.
 This followed an almost identical failure reported in 2024 by Drive Safe and Fast , which also showed another Omoda 5 with a disconnected rear axle.
 Chery Omoda 5 with its rear axle partially torn out. Image credit: Drive Safe and Fast The faults and subsequent investigations by Chery have now prompted a recall of the Omoda 5, impacting Australian-delivered examples.
 “Due to a manufacturing defect, the rear axle assembly may have been insufficiently welded and could crack. If this occurs, it could lead to a loss of vehicle control,” Chery said in its recall notice .
 “A loss of vehicle control will increase the risk of an accident which may cause injury or death to vehicle occupants and other road users.”
 Chery Omoda 5 
 While the Chery Omoda 5 has subsequently been renamed as the Chery C5, the newer model isn’t impacted, as it has moved from the torsion-beam rear suspension layout of the Omoda 5 to an independent rear suspension setup.
 Chery dealers will inspect whether potentially affected Omoda 5s are fitted with a rear axle from a specific supplier during a particular period. Cars which do not have the potentially faulty parts will not need a replacement.
 For more information, owners can contact the Chery Motor Australia Customer Service Team on 1800 424 379 or by emailing [email protected] .
